p2p.note: Counts every lc_msg frame posted by the local BroadcastChannel transport (wrapper on BroadcastChannel.prototype.postMessage); a host broadcast counts once per recipient. Bytes = UTF-8 length of JSON.stringify(payload). Production uses PeerJS with binary serialization, so these JSON sizes are an approximation; PeerJS framing, WebRTC/ICE and signaling traffic are not included. Headless Chromium, one page, all players in-page. Control frames (lc_connect/lc_accept/lc_bye/lc_kick) are not counted as messages. The per-op scenarios use host + 2 guests: one acting guest and one observer.

youtube.note: Simulated with a fake fetch and fake timers; no network and no key. Units are the client own counter (sessionUnits): 1 per videos.list (verify, once) and 5 per liveChat/messages request (poll). Real Google billing is per request by these same unit costs, but the client does not account for other API calls (search, other tabs or apps sharing the key). The daily quota resets at midnight Pacific time. The 1-hour window starts at the first poll (t = 0) and includes the poll at t = 60 min. "Hours per day" = (10,000 - verify units) / polling units per hour, i.e. one verify per day plus continuous polling.

client.note: Numbers are from headless Chromium on this machine (no GPU guarantees, no real device); use them to compare versions, not as absolute performance. startupMs = GameSession.startNewPuzzle() (engine.initPuzzle plus session setup) on a seeded sample image. frame ms = wall time of one renderFrame call with requestRender() before it, so each call redraws; canvas 2D work may be partly deferred by the browser and not fully visible in this time. 120 frames per case, with now advancing 1000/60 ms per frame. Heap numbers come from performance.memory when available (Chromium, coarse, includes garbage not yet collected). Chromium quantizes performance.memory, so small heap deltas read as 0; treat heap numbers as indicative only. Frame ms that read 0 are real: those frames drew little (see firstFrameMs for the build cost).
